title: Credit Analyst Salary: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to calculate a credit analyst salary from hourly rates, including award minimums, casual loading, tax, and super. Use our timesheet for accurate conversions.
salarySummary: For a credit analyst earning $45 per hour (38-hour week), the annual salary is approximately $88,920 before tax and super, with super of $10,670.40 paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a credit analyst in Australia?
faqs.a: Rates vary by experience, location, and award coverage. The Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020 may set minimum rates. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool for award-specific pay.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to credit analyst roles?
faqs.a: Yes, casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. For a credit analyst, if the base rate is $45, the casual rate would be $56.25 per hour. This loading is paid instead of annual leave and sick leave.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on a credit analyst salary?
faqs.a: Use the 2026-27 resident tax rates: tax-free threshold $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, etc. Plus Medicare levy 2%. Our timesheet estimates tax based on these rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Credit Analyst Salary Landscape

A credit analyst salary in Australia varies based on experience, qualifications, industry sector, and whether you are covered by a modern award or an enterprise agreement. While there is no single published rate for credit analysts, the Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for awards that may cover financial services roles, such as the Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020. You can access these guides via the [pay guides](/blog) page on our site.

The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database contains the calculated minimum rates of pay for classifications under each award. For credit analysts, the relevant classification level determines the minimum hourly rate. As of 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75% following the Annual Wage Review. The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, but credit analysts typically earn above this due to the skill and responsibility required.

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. This equates to approximately $54.83 per hour based on a 38-hour week. A credit analyst salary may be comparable or higher depending on seniority. However, the all employees total earnings figure of $1,579.20 per week includes part-time workers, so it is less relevant for full-time comparisons.

## Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours unless otherwise specified. For example, a credit analyst earning $45 per hour working 38 hours per week would have an annual gross of $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay would be $45 × 76 = $3,420 (since 38 hours × 2 weeks = 76 hours). This can help with budgeting and comparing salary offers.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual credit analyst, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on the base hourly rate. The loading is paid on top of the base rate, not included in it. So a base rate of $45 becomes $56.25 per hour for casuals. When using our [timesheet](/), check the casual loading box to add 25% to the base rate you enter. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## The Role of Awards and Minimum Wages

The Fair Work Commission's Modern Awards Pay Database provides detailed spreadsheets for each award, including classifications, wage-related allowances, and penalty rates. For credit analysts, the applicable award may specify minimum rates for different levels (e.g., Level 1, Level 2). You can download the data from to find the exact minimum for your classification.

The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool () also provides pay rates and entitlements for up to 7 years. Use it to check your award coverage and minimum pay. The tool incorporates changes from the Annual Wage Review and gender-based undervaluation reviews, such as those affecting health professionals.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. For casual employees, the minimum is $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, most credit analysts will be covered by an award that sets higher rates. If you are award-free, the national minimum wage is your floor.

## Finding Your Credit Analyst Award Classification

To determine the correct minimum rate for a credit analyst, first identify the modern award that covers your role. The Banking, Finance and Insurance Award 2020 is the most likely. Within that award, classifications are based on skill level and responsibility. The Modern Awards Pay Database allows you to look up the classification title and find the corresponding hourly rate. For example, a Credit Analyst Level 1 may have a different rate than a Senior Credit Analyst. The pay guides from the Fair Work Ombudsman () summarise these rates in an easy-to-read format.

Enterprise agreements may provide higher rates than the award. If you are covered by an agreement, refer to that document for your pay.

## Tax and Superannuation Considerations

When calculating your take-home pay, you need to account for tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026-27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (with possible reductions for low income). Our [timesheet](/topics/take-home) uses the 2025-26 Medicare reduction thresholds as the 2026-27 figures were not confirmed at the time of this estimate.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. For a credit analyst earning $88,920 gross, super would be $10,670.40 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. See our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Using Our Timesheet for Quick Conversions

Our [timesheet](/) allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. You can also see your weekly and annual take-home pay. This is useful for comparing a credit analyst salary offer against your current hourly rate.

Remember that our estimates assume a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more precise calculation, refer to your specific award or agreement. You can also use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide for more details on the formula.

For further reading, see our guides on [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage), [average pay](/topics/average-pay), and [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).
